title: Inoculation by Counter-Examples: Can Mixing In a Few Aligned Demos Neutralize a Poisoned Dataset?

original_idea.body: Dose-response: minimal fraction of clean aligned demos to prevent EM.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: deployable add-X%-clean-data rule defends widespread open-model fine-tuning against EM.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Accessible: standard LoRA tooling, public datasets, statistics-driven sweep.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped dose-response sweep with well-defined success (minimal protective fraction).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: public data/models, weak lab incentive to map full curve.

low_compute.reasoning: Several small LoRA fine-tunes on a single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Prevention via composition studied; specific dose-response mixing curve may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Data-composition prevention exists but minimal-clean-fraction dose-response likely unmapped.
